articles.title: Asia's Underground Water Is Disappearing Fast, Scientists Warn
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that the region known as Asia's 'Water Tower' — the high-altitude areas that supply freshwater to billions of people across the continent — is losing about 24.2 billion tonnes of underground water every single year. The worst drops are happening in busy farming areas where many people live. Researchers say that melting glaciers might slow the problem for a short time around the 2060s, but if people do not change the way they use water, things will get much worse. This is a serious warning about the future of drinking and farming water across Asia.

lv1: What is Asia's 'Water Tower' and why is it important for people? (亞洲的「水塔」是什麼，為什麼對人們很重要？)
How many billion tonnes of underground water does Asia lose every year? (亞洲每年流失多少億噸地下水？)
lv2: Why might melting glaciers only help the water shortage problem for a short time, and not fix it permanently? (為什麼冰川融化只能暫時緩解缺水問題，而不能永久解決？)
How does the way farmers use water affect the amount of underground water available for everyone? (農民的用水方式如何影響所有人可使用的地下水量？)
lv3: Who should be most responsible for reducing water use in Asia — governments, farmers, or ordinary citizens — and why? (誰應該為減少亞洲用水量負上最大責任——政府、農民還是普通市民？為什麼？)
If underground water in Asia runs out, which groups of people do you think will suffer most, and is that fair? (如果亞洲地下水耗盡，你認為哪些群體會受到最大的衝擊？這公平嗎？)

articles.source: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
articles.title: People Around the World Are Trusting the News Less, New Report Finds
articles.summary: A major new report on how people read the news shows that audiences across the world are feeling more and more uneasy about what is happening around them. Big changes in technology, world trade, and politics are making people question things they once took for granted. The report also found that artificial intelligence is now spreading quickly into everyday life, and more and more people feel overwhelmed by the sheer amount of news they see on their phones every day. Trust in news organisations has fallen in many countries, with people worried about whether the information they receive is reliable and honest.

lv1: According to the report, are people around the world trusting the news more or less than before? (根據報告，全球人們對新聞的信任度是增加了還是減少了？)
What new technology does the report mention that is changing how people get their news? (報告提到哪種新科技正在改變人們獲取新聞的方式？)
lv2: Why might people feel 'overloaded' by news on their smartphones, and how could this affect what they choose to believe? (為什麼人們可能會對智能手機上的新聞感到「超負荷」？這又會如何影響他們的判斷？)
Why is it a problem if trust in news organisations falls in many countries at the same time? (如果許多國家同時出現對新聞機構信任度下降的情況，這會帶來什麼問題？)
lv3: Do you think AI-generated news makes it harder or easier for people to find the truth, and what can young people do to protect themselves from misinformation? (你認為人工智能生成的新聞是否令人們更難找到真相？年輕人可以怎樣保護自己免受虛假資訊的影響？)
Should governments be allowed to control what news people can read online in order to fight misinformation? What are the risks of doing this? (政府是否應該被允許管控人們在網上閱讀的新聞內容以打擊虛假資訊？這樣做有什麼風險？)

articles.title: 聖保羅書院IAL放榜 16人奪狀元 6人達5A*「超級狀元」
articles.summary: 香港聖保羅書院公布2026年英國高級程度文憑（IAL）考試成績，全校共有16名同學榮獲狀元殊榮。當中6人在五個科目全獲A*最高評級，成為「超級狀元」，另外10人則考獲四個A*。IAL是英國廣受認可的國際考試，成績優秀有助同學申請英國、香港及世界各地的大學。今年成績突出，反映同學努力備考，亦顯示學校的學術水平備受肯定。

lv1: 聖保羅書院今年共有多少名同學成為IAL狀元？
「超級狀元」需要在幾個科目考獲A*才可達到這個稱號？
lv2: IAL成績優秀對同學升讀大學有什麼幫助？為什麼這對他們的未來很重要？
為什麼學校的狀元人數多少，會被視為反映該校整體學術水平的指標？
lv3: 只以考試成績來判斷一個學生是否優秀，你認為這樣公平嗎？還有哪些能力同樣重要？
香港學生修讀IAL等國際考試課程，與修讀本地DSE課程相比，各有什麼優勢和不足？

articles.title: 南韓濟州島警員偽造失蹤案報告 3日內4具遺體相繼被發現
articles.summary: 南韓濟州島發生嚴重警察失職事件。當地在短短三天內，先後發現四名失蹤人士的遺體，調查後揭發涉事警員曾擅自竄改報告，謊稱失蹤者「平安無事」並私自關閉案件，導致搜救工作嚴重延誤。事件震驚全國，南韓總統李在明強烈譴責警隊「紀律鬆散」，宣布下令徹查事件，並要求總理研究全面改革警察制度的方案。

lv1: 南韓濟州島的警員做了什麼錯誤的事情？
南韓總統對這次警察失職事件有什麼反應？
lv2: 警員私自關閉失蹤案件，為什麼會導致搜救工作延誤，並對失蹤者家屬造成傷害？
為什麼社會對警察的誠信和責任感有很高的要求？警察失去市民信任會帶來什麼後果？
lv3: 當執法人員違規失職時，應該由誰來監察和追究他們的責任？現有的制度是否足夠？
這次事件反映出警察制度可能存在什麼系統性問題？你認為怎樣的改革才能真正防止類似事件再次發生？
